description:
**The Unarchiver 4.3.9 works well in Darling: it extracts archives, shows its progress window, asks for passwords and remembers its settings.** I found only small problems, listed below.

I installed it the usual way: the disk image mounts with `hdiutil attach`, and the app is dragged into `/Applications`. On the very first launch you get the privacy policy and terms window; after pressing Accept the app is ready (it has no main window, it works on the archives you give it).

What works:
- **Extracting:** zip, 7z, rar and tar.gz archives (each with a folder and a few files), given to the app when it starts, all extracted next to the archive with the right contents. A 7z of about 250 MB showed the progress window with a filling blue bar and the name of the current file, and all the files were there at the end.
- **Password-protected zip:** the prompt appears, shows the typed password as bullets, and after Continue the archive is extracted.
- **File > Unarchive to Current Folder...:** the file dialog has its sidebar, folder pop-up, back and forward buttons and a striped file list. I switched folders with the sidebar and with the Go to the folder sheet (Cmd+Shift+G, type a path, Go), picked an archive and pressed Unarchive, and it was extracted. Cancel closes the dialog and the app stays responsive, and I could open the dialog again.
- **Settings:** all four tabs (Archive Formats, Extraction, Advanced, Analytics) look right and the controls respond. I changed an option on the Extraction tab, quit with Cmd+Q, started the app again, and the option was still changed.
- **Menus:** the menu bar menus open and highlight the item under the pointer.

What does not work or is not quite right:
- "Reveal expanded item(s) in Finder" does nothing (there is no Finder), so the extracted folder is not opened after extraction. It does not show an error either.
- When I gave the app archives on its command line, it stayed running after the extraction, as Mac apps do, but its menu bar disappeared when the progress window closed, so there was no way to quit it and I had to kill it from outside. I did not try opening archives through the file manager.
- The long text on the Analytics tab is still cut off after two lines.

I did not try dragging archives onto the window.

Tested on Arch Linux with X11, with a Darling build from mid November 2026.
